title: Fixed early fits at 13.2543 days reduce late GJ 3293 error in A88 velocities but increase it in SERVAL
abstract: We test a known weak radial velocity signal in public HARPS data for GJ 3293. Early fits at the fixed 13.2543-day period reduce last-season squared error by 10.45 percent in the 2017 A88 velocities. They increase error by 1.51 percent in corrected SERVAL velocities and by 1.94 percent without the nightly correction. The sign of each result persists across 12 baseline and weight choices. Block resampling ranges include zero. A matched-date check retains the product comparison. Eight G2-mask DRS records have a large offset; an early-fitted mask offset reduces the DRS prediction error from 67.67 to 3.81 m/s. Early-only period searches, yearly aliases, a rotation harmonic and activity indicators give no secure physical attribution. The products share spectra, and the fixed published periods used the full historical data. This is a conditional model test, not independent confirmation or rejection of the known planet. We report no new planet or phenomenon. Code, selected data, exact raw hashes, figures and offline instructions are included.
